items.t: MetLife stock posts record adjusted EPS as legal exposure lingers
sum: MetLife reported its third-quarter 2026 results on Wednesday, November 4, with record adjusted earnings per share and revenue growth across all six business segments. The company said adjusted earnings rose 12 percent to 1.8 billion US dollars, while adjusted earnings per share excluding notable items increased 22 percent to 2.85 US dollars.

The results were published in a MetLife Business Wire release for the quarter ended September 30. Premiums, fees and other revenues rose 12 percent to 14.1 billion US dollars, while adjusted premiums, fees and other revenues excluding pension risk transfers increased 8 percent to 13.5 billion US dollars.

Group Benefits adjusted earnings rose 15 percent to 523 million US dollars. Retirement and Income Solutions posted adjusted earnings of 413 million US dollars, down 6 percent on a reported basis, but earnings excluding notable items increased 12 percent to 478 million US dollars. Asia, Latin America, Europe, the Middle East and Africa, and MetLife Investment Management also reported higher adjusted earnings.

The release said the annual actuarial assumption review reduced adjusted earnings by 46 million US dollars. Excluding total notable items, adjusted earnings reached 1.826 billion US dollars, compared with 1.566 billion US dollars in the prior-year quarter.

Separately, the Ontario Superior Court of Justice approved a 213.5 million Canadian dollar settlement on October 27 related to certain life insurance policies originally sold by Metropolitan Life Insurance Company in Canada. The Advisor.ca report said the agreement covers about 70,000 current and former policyholders and includes compensation and limits on selected policy charges. Sun Life administers the policies and has said it would seek recovery from MetLife under an indemnity arrangement.
MetLife stock traded at 88.19 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 11:14 CET on Saturday, November 7, 2026.

For investors, the quarter highlights earnings momentum from underwriting, investment income and volume growth, while the Canadian case keeps historical policy obligations on the agenda. The company also said it returned approximately 1 billion US dollars to shareholders through repurchases and common stock dividends.

MetLife stock: Record adjusted EPS meets broad segment growth
sum: MetLife reported a strong third quarter on Wednesday, November 4, after the US market close, with record adjusted earnings per share excluding total notable items. The insurer's official third-quarter release said adjusted EPS reached 2.85 US dollars, the highest quarterly level in company history.

Net income rose 187 percent year over year to 2.4 billion US dollars, or 3.67 US dollars per share. Adjusted earnings increased 12 percent to 1.8 billion US dollars, supported by higher variable investment income, broad-based volume growth and favorable underwriting.

Premiums, fees and other revenues increased 12 percent to 14.1 billion US dollars. Adjusted premiums, fees and other revenues excluding pension risk transfers rose 8 percent to 13.5 billion US dollars, with growth in all six business segments. The figures indicate that the quarter's operating expansion was not limited to one division.

Adjusted return on equity reached 19.6 percent excluding total notable items. MetLife also returned approximately 1 billion US dollars through share repurchases and common stock dividends, while holding-company cash and liquid assets totaled 3.4 billion US dollars at quarter-end.

MetLife said it remains on track to deliver its full-year free cash flow ratio and direct expense ratio targets. Chief Executive Michel Khalaf described the quarter as evidence of the New Frontier strategy's execution and said management remains confident that it can produce repeatable results.
The real-time quote of MetLife stock was 88.69 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 16:39 CET on Friday, November 6, 2026.

MetLife stock posts record adjusted EPS in third quarter
sum: MetLife announced its third-quarter 2026 results on Wednesday, November 4, after the US market close. In its official release, the insurer reported record quarterly adjusted earnings per share of 2.85 US dollars excluding total notable items.

Net income increased 187 percent year over year to 2.4 billion US dollars, or 3.67 US dollars per share. Adjusted earnings rose 12 percent to 1.8 billion US dollars. MetLife said higher variable investment income, broad-based volume growth and favorable underwriting supported the result.

Premiums, fees and other revenues increased 12 percent to 14.1 billion US dollars. Adjusted premiums, fees and other revenues excluding pension risk transfers rose 8 percent to 13.5 billion US dollars, with growth in all six business segments. The figures point to a broad-based expansion rather than a result driven by a single division.

Total return on equity was 42.7 percent, while adjusted return on equity stood at 19.2 percent. Excluding total notable items, adjusted return on equity reached 19.6 percent. MetLife also reported adjusted book value per share of 59.41 US dollars, up 5 percent, while reported book value per share fell 22 percent to 30.73 US dollars.

Chief Executive Michel Khalaf said the quarter demonstrated the strength of MetLife's New Frontier strategy and the discipline of its execution. He pointed to revenue growth in every business segment, solid underwriting, volume growth and higher investment returns. Management also said it remained confident that the strategy can deliver repeatable results and confirmed progress toward its full-year free cash flow ratio and direct expense ratio targets.

MetLife returned approximately 1 billion US dollars to shareholders through share repurchases and common stock dividends. Holding-company cash and liquid assets stood at 3.4 billion US dollars at the end of the quarter, within the company's target range.

Analysts covering the company have generally reconfirmed their estimates over the last 30 days, suggesting they anticipate the business will stay the course heading into earnings. MetLife has missed Wall Street’s revenue estimates multiple times over the last two years.

MetLife stock heads into earnings with 2.71 US dollar EPS consensus
sum: MetLife is heading into a closely watched earnings date after analysts raised their expectations for the insurer's third quarter. Yahoo Finance reported on October 24 that the company is expected to publish fiscal 2026 third-quarter results after the US market close on Wednesday, November 4.

Analysts tracked in the preview expect diluted earnings per share of 2.71 US dollars, up from 2.34 US dollars in the year-earlier quarter. The projected increase would extend a recent run of outperformance: MetLife exceeded consensus estimates in each of the four preceding quarters, according to the same report.

The upcoming release will give investors a new reading on the insurer's earnings power across life insurance, employee benefits, annuities, retirement solutions and investment management. Yahoo Finance described MetLife as a global financial services company operating in more than 40 markets, with exposure to the United States, Asia, Latin America, Europe and the Middle East.

For full-year 2026, analysts cited in the preview expect earnings per share of 9.94 US dollars, compared with 8.89 US dollars in fiscal 2025. The forecast for fiscal 2027 stands at 10.72 US dollars, implying that the market is looking for continued earnings growth beyond the next quarterly release.

The comparison with recent operating trends is important for investors. Over the five years covered by the report, net premiums earned increased at an annual rate of 2.7%, while earnings per share rose at an annual rate of 3.3%. The third-quarter figures will show whether current earnings momentum is keeping pace with those longer-term trends.

Capital returns provide another date for shareholders to monitor. MetLife's board declared a fourth-quarter 2026 cash dividend of 0.5925 US dollars per common share on October 6, according to the Yahoo Finance report. The dividend is scheduled to be paid on December 8 to shareholders of record on November 3.

The record date falls one day before the earnings release, placing the distribution schedule alongside the principal earnings catalyst. For the stock, the key issues after the report will be whether results exceed the 2.71 US dollar EPS hurdle and whether management's outlook supports the estimates for 2026 and 2027.

items.t: Raiders Stock Report: Risers & Fallers After Thrilling Win Over Jets
sum: The Las Vegas Raiders entered their Week 8 matchup against the New York Jets desperately needing a win. After four straight games against the league's top teams, the Jets were, on paper, the team Las Vegas needed to get back on track after a tough few weeks.

Week 8 was supposed to be a manageable game for a Raiders team that has one of the league's toughest schedules. Las Vegas' road slate against the Jets is sandwiched between games against multiple teams with Super Bowl aspirations.
Las Vegas' offense woke up just in time to pull out a thrilling victory against the Jets on Sunday. Their defense played a solid second half, holding New York to 10 second-half points.

Falling behind early and trying their hardest to come back in the second half is becoming the Raiders' identity. Below are the players who are rising and falling after the Raiders' Week 8 loss to the Jets, their fifth straight loss.

Despite many narratives, Las Vegas' offensive line entered Week 8 in the top 10-15 in several statistical categories. The unit excelled significantly more in pass-blocking than in run-blocking. On Sunday, the unit excelled in both, helping Las Vegas jump out to an early lead.

The unit has its deficiencies, but when it comes to giving the quarterback enough time to throw the ball or escape the pocket and make a play, Las Vegas' offensive line plays well. Las Vegas' ground game was its most efficient in weeks because the line played well overall on Sunday.

Nailor's numbers have not shown the true impact he has on the Raiders' offense. However, Nailor's absence noticeably strained the unit in Week 6. His return made a subtle but significant difference for Las Vegas' offense in Week 7, opening things up, despite his lack of stats.

items.t: Here is Why MetLife (MET) is One of the Best Value Stocks to Buy Right Now
sum: MetLife Inc. (NYSE:MET) is one of the best value stocks to buy right now. On June 11, MetLife launched the Non-Qualified Assignment Flex Agreement/NQA-FA to provide more flexible settlement options for non-physical injury claims. Unlike traditional structures, this funding agreement allows for deferred payments extending beyond one year, enabling customized schedules for diverse cases like employment disputes and contract litigation.

The NQA-FA grants attorneys and brokers greater control over payment timing and design for both individual and business payees. By using a funding agreement rather than a standard annuity, it bypasses traditional regulatory restrictions, offering a versatile tool that adapts to the specific financial needs of claimants.

This solution directly addresses the rising demand for adaptable settlement structures in an era of increasingly complex litigation. By combining payment flexibility with MetLife Inc.'s (NYSE:MET) financial guarantees, the NQA-FA aims to support long-term financial security for those involved in legal settlements.

MetLife Inc. (NYSE:MET) provides insurance and financial services to individual and institutional clients in the US, Latin America, EMEA, and Japan. The company is based in New York, New York, and was founded in March 1868.
